title: The audit requirement covers on-chain code only — off-chain services and user interfaces are excluded by default
content:
A.1.10.2.7.1 requires an audit "before new smart contract code is introduced to the Sky Ecosystem," covering "smart contracts and module onboardings" and "deployment and initialization scripts required to deploy and configure smart contracts." It then draws the boundary: "**This requirement does not extend to other code, such as off-chain services or user interfaces, unless separately specified.**"

The rationale is presumably that on-chain code is immutable and directly controls funds, while off-chain code can be patched. That holds for a class of failures but not for all of them.

A compromised frontend does not need to break the protocol to cause loss — it needs only to present a different transaction than the user believes they are signing. Sky's own Accessibility Scope covers frontends and distribution, and the Executive Process depends on off-chain systems throughout: the Voting Portal that displays proposals, the validation tool, the Executive Validator preview, keeper infrastructure. None of that is inside this audit requirement.

The escape clause — "unless separately specified" — means other parts of the Atlas may impose requirements elsewhere, and the Governance Scope simply is not where they live. So this is a scope statement rather than a claim that such code is unaudited.

Still, it is worth noting precisely because the audit requirement is invoked as a gate throughout the Executive and Prime Spell processes. "It has been audited" in those contexts means the on-chain artifact was reviewed, and nothing about the surrounding software that users and voters actually interact with.
description: A.1.10.2.7.1 mandates audits for smart contracts, module onboardings and deployment scripts, then explicitly disclaims other code 'unless separately specified'.
